description: Vendor datasheet pump curves used as labelled reference equipment scenarios. Every value here is a datasheet table entry or a manual graph reading, not a measured confidence interval, and no wet, hot or degraded performance is claimed.

knf_n922_ste_50hz.name: KNF N 922 STE IP 54, 230 V 50 Hz capacitor motor
knf_n922_ste_50hz.role: Reference equipment screen for the prototype pump. Not a selected final pump, and not a validated prediction of system performance.

source.document: KNF N 922 ST IP 54 datasheet, 082024 (page 1 ratings, page 2 curves)
source.curve_used: black 50 Hz curve, vacuum half only (left of the atmospheric split). The blue 60 Hz curve, the dashed intermittent curve and the compressor half of the chart are not used.
source.page_2_table: Steady-state page-2 table repeats 21.0 +/- 10 % l/min at atmospheric pressure, 6.0/87.0 bar rel/psig, 110 mbar abs ultimate vacuum, with the footnote 'Flow rate determined at 20 C, 1013 mbar abs (pressure 0 to 1013 mbar abs in accordance with ISO 21360-1/2)'.

digitization.method: manual column-wise extraction of the black curve from the page render, calibrated on the detected grey gridlines (4.85 hPa per pixel horizontally, 0.145 l/min per pixel vertically)
digitization.pixel_limits: approximately +/- 0.3 l/min and +/- 5 hPa from pixel resolution and line thickness
digitization.status: graph reading for screening use; not a measured uncertainty and not a vendor tabulated data file

annotations.110.0: Pinned to the datasheet ultimate vacuum of 110 mbar abs; the digitized curve merges with the axis between about 110 and 136 hPa.
annotations.150.0: Digitized; lowest clean point above the axis merge.
annotations.985.0: Digitized 20.37 l/min; beyond this the black and blue curves overlap in the render.
annotations.1013.25: Datasheet performance table value 21.0 +/- 10 % at atmospheric pressure, used instead of the last few overlapped pixels.

flow_model.basis: Reference-condition volumetric throughput Q_ref(P) at 101300 Pa and 293.15 K. Bench volumetric speed at the pump inlet is S(P) = Q_ref(P) * P_ref / P, and the molar throughput is S(P) * P / (R * T) = Q_ref(P) * P_ref / (R * T).
flow_model.why_reference_basis: The footnote alone only states the conditions at which the flow was determined; treating the plotted volume as the volume at the current inlet pressure would make the mass flow fall towards zero as the inlet pressure falls. That inference is checked for graphical consistency against the 20 L vessel pump-down curve printed on the same page: the reference basis reaches 200 mbar in 2.18 min against 2.28 min digitized (-4 %, inside the chart's graphical resolution and consistent with the datasheet's +/- 10 % flow rating at atmospheric pressure, which is a rating at one point rather than an error band on the whole curve), while the inlet-volume basis needs 5.98 min (2.6x too slow). One published vendor curve is a consistency check, not a validation set. The reference basis is adopted on that evidence, not on the footnote wording.
flow_model.temperature_transfer: Assumption, not measurement: the pump is treated as a fixed-throughput device, so carrying the bench volumetric speed to another gas temperature keeps S(P) and re-evaluates the molar flow with the local density. Gas composition (CO2-rich wet vacuum gas versus air) is assumed not to change the curve; no wet or hot calibration is claimed.
flow_model.curve_domain: Tabulated from 110 hPa to 1013.25 hPa absolute. Above the top of the map the top-of-map value is held and the run is flagged as unsupported extrapolation; at or below the ultimate pressure the flow is exactly zero, which is not by itself an invalidity condition because the cooling bed can lower its own pressure with the pump valve closed.

electrical.basis: Constant running input assumption: the datasheet rated input P1, 50 Hz = 135 W is counted whenever the pump is on, including when the suction valve is throttled closed. This is a rated value, not a measured pressure-power curve.
electrical.throttle_note: Valve throttling changes the gas path only. It is not motor-speed control and does not scale the electrical input.
electrical.future_curve: A tabulated electrical-power map (pressure_Pa, power_W arrays) can replace this assumption without changing the flow model; the loader validates such a map for monotone pressures, finiteness and nonnegative power.
electrical.reference: https://knf.com/fileadmin/Global_files/Downloads/Product_OEM_Process/Datasheets/Datasheet_N_922_ST_IP54_082024_Web.pdf (page 1, ELECTRICAL DATA: Power P1, 50 Hz (W) 135; Imax 0.62 A)

pumpdown_check.curve: black 50 Hz curve of the page-2 'PUMP DOWN TIME FOR 20 LITER VESSEL' panel
pumpdown_check.tolerance: unit test uses 15 % on the digitized anchor; the two interpretations differ by a factor of 2.6, so the test separates them
pumpdown_check.limitation: The datasheet pump-down is a single vendor-published curve on one unspecified 20 L vessel, so the match is graphical consistency only and not a validated error band on the curve.

annotations.operating_scope: With no inlet cooler, line or condenser model, the gas entering the pump is assumed to be at the bed temperature. That exceeds the 60 C media limit during desorption, so the reference case is flagged as an equipment screen rather than a viable design; no ideal cooler is inserted.
annotations.scheduling: Shared-utility checks distinguish the requested equivalent capacity (valve open, reference-condition throughput) from the valve-dependent effective speed actually delivered.
